uncited: Analytical vector fields generate flow data using explicit mathematical functions of position and time, rather than retrieving values from pre-computed simulation grids or particle systems.
This approach solves the problem of obtaining velocity vectors for procedural volume rendering where simulation data is unavailable or too expensive to compute in real-time.

Unlike [Vortex Flow Function](2538-vortex-flow-function.md), which models specific swirling motion around a cylinder, or [Smoke Column with Helical Displacement](2743-smoke-column-with-helical-displacement.md), which applies geometric displacement, analytical fields provide a general framework where any vector is determined by evaluating a function $\nu(\mathbf{v}, t)$ at a given point $\mathbf{v}$ and time $t$.
The core mechanism of analytical vector fields is the evaluation of a deterministic function that maps a 3D spatial coordinate and a time parameter to a 3D velocity vector.
To simulate particle motion or advect volume data, the vector field is integrated over time steps.
This family includes specific implementations that define the function $\nu(\mathbf{v}, t)$ using different mathematical constructs.
A constant vector field where the output vector is independent of the input position.

A common approach for real-time behavior is the fourth-order Runge-Kutta method (RK4), which estimates the position $\mathbf{x}_{i+1}$ at time $t + \delta$ from $\mathbf{x}_i$ at time $t$ using four samples of the vector field in the neighborhood of $\mathbf{x}_i$ [S1, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states that the chosen approach for real-time behavior involves taking four samples from the underlying vector field in the neighborhood of the current position to calculate the next position. It further defines this method as the Fourth-order Runge-Kutta (RK4) method, providing the specific formula $x_{i+1} = x_i +  rac{1}{6}  eta (v_0 + 2v_1 + 2v_2 + v_3)$ which utilizes four sample values ($v_0$ through $v_3$). This aligns perfectly with the claim that RK4 estimates position using four samples of the vector field.
